title: Procureur général detains First President of the Cour de Cassation in Fonds souverain inquiry
author: Hélène Vasseur, correspondante judiciaire — Agence des Républiques (ADR)
partialContent: The procureur général has ordered the detention of Élisabeth Vaugelas, First President of the Cour de Cassation, over the alleged suppression of a référé and the transfer of sealed documents in the Fonds souverain inquiry. The Conseil supérieur de la magistrature met in an emergency session and the Assemblée des Républiques has summoned the Minister of Justice for an interpellation this afternoon.

title: Banque des Républiques raises taux directeur to 5.75 per cent as livre pressure persists
author: Marc-Antoine Rivière, rubrique économique — Agence Continentale
partialContent: The Banque des Républiques raised its taux directeur by half a point to 5.75 per cent, the fourth increase in twelve months, citing services inflation above 4 per cent. Governor Marguerite Salvat confirmed two recent interventions to steady the livre, while the government signalled that infrastructure spending may be trimmed.

title: Conseil constitutionnel censures surveillance loi, citing libertés fondamentales
author: Agence des Républiques (ADR)
partialContent: The Conseil constitutionnel has struck down two central articles of the loi sur la surveillance numérique, ruling that twenty-four months of bulk data retention was disproportionate. The decision, taken seven votes to four, leaves the framework for targeted interception intact but forces the government to revise its implementation décret.

title: Ministère de l’Éducation sets out baccalauréat reform for the 2028 session
author: Nadia Belrose, correspondante éducation, bureau d’Aurelle — Presses de Vallonne
partialContent: The ministry has presented a baccalauréat reform that shifts 40 per cent of the final mark to continuous assessment and reduces the number of written papers from six to four. Teachers’ unions are divided, with one calling a préavis de grève for 12 November, while six académies will pilot the system from the 2026 rentrée.

title: Cour des comptes audit traces undisclosed tranches in Fonds souverain accounts
author: Théodore Marchetti, enquête économique — Agence Économique d’Aurelle (AEA)
partialContent: A draft audit by the Cour des comptes identifies nine tranches of the Fonds souverain, worth 6.4 billion livres, placed through intermediary companies in Vallonne between 2022 and 2025. The auditors criticise the fund’s internal controls and recommend suspending two senior officials pending an administrative inquiry.

title: Tribunal administratif widens force majeure doctrine in flood-liability arrêt
author: Inès Rouvier, chronique judiciaire — Presses de Vallonne
partialContent: The Tribunal administratif d’Aurelle has ruled that repeated flooding in the Vallonne valley can no longer be treated as unforeseeable, restricting the force majeure exception invoked by insurers. The insurers’ federation will appeal to the Conseil d’État against a judgment that could expose the industry to 220 million livres in claims.

title: Académies rely on intérimaires as thousands of teaching posts stay unfilled
author: Texte : Gaël Fontaine, correspondant éducation — Presses de Vallonne · Photographies : Rémi Chastel — Agence Continentale
partialContent: More than 4,100 teaching posts remain unfilled six weeks after the rentrée, and six académies have waived the concours requirement to hire intérimaires for up to a full school year.

title: Bourse d’Aurelle closes at record high as energy exports lift earnings
author: Agence Continentale — bureau de la Bourse d’Aurelle
partialContent: The Indice d’Aurelle closed at a record 12,486 points, up 1.4 per cent, as four of the largest energy exporters reported better-than-expected results and announced new supply contracts. Analysts warn that five firms now account for 38 per cent of the index, leaving the market exposed to a single political decision on export tariffs.

title: Cour de Cassation curbs garde à vue extensions for minor offences
author: Étienne Bréart, chronique judiciaire — Agence des Républiques (ADR)
partialContent: The criminal chamber has ruled that extensions of garde à vue in minor-offence cases must rest on concrete and individualised grounds set out in writing by the procureur. The barreau d’Aurelle welcomes a ruling that ends a decade of automatic extensions, while victims’ associations warn of slower investigations.

title: Conseil d’État to rule on school-attire décret in laïcité dispute
author: Texte : Margot Delaunay — Agence des Républiques (ADR) · Photographies : Lucie Sorbier — Presses de Vallonne
partialContent: The Conseil d’État will rule next month on a décret extending laïcité rules to municipal extracurricular activities, challenged by a parents’ collectif through a référé. The rapporteur public has recommended rejecting the challenge while noting that the boundary between school time and municipal activities deserves clarification from the legislature.

title: Avocats du Barreau d’Aurelle announce three-day strike over aide juridictionnelle
author: Jeanne Vasseur, correspondante judiciaire — Agence des Républiques (ADR)
partialContent: The Conseil de l’ordre voted to suspend hearings for three days from 3 November after the aide juridictionnelle tariff was left unchanged for a fourth year. Urgences, gardes à vue and detention hearings remain covered by a minimum service.

title: Parquet de Vallonne opens inquiry after scellés vanish from the sealed-evidence room
author: Paul Rémond, reporter — Agence Continentale
partialContent: A routine inventory found four sealed boxes from a narcotics case missing from the tribunal’s evidence room in Vallonne. The parquet has opened an enquête préliminaire and the syndicat de la magistrature demands the room’s camera logs.

title: Conseil supérieur de la magistrature reprimands procureur over flood-dossier delays
author: Hélène Vasseur, correspondante judiciaire — Agence des Républiques (ADR)
partialContent: The Conseil supérieur de la magistrature found that expert conclusions in the flood-liability proceedings went without instruction for fourteen months. The procureur, short of two substituts, has been asked to submit a plan de renfort before December.

title: Cour de Cassation upholds sale of the former préfecture of Marbre to a private fonds
author: Marc-Antoine Rivière, rédacteur économique — Agence Continentale
partialContent: The civil chamber rejected the département de Marbre’s pourvoi against the 2023 sale of its former préfecture to a private fonds, ending a conflit de compétence between the two orders. Opposition councillors announce a recours before the Cour européenne.

title: Assemblée opens debate on a national register of garde à vue
author: Sophie Delorme, correspondante parlementaire — Presses de Vallonne
partialContent: The proposed loi would log every garde à vue within the hour, with the identity of the officier de police judiciaire and the written grounds for extensions. The ministère de l’Intérieur warns of a cost of 30 million livres.
